fieldValues.title: An essay writer can format text only by knowing markdown, and nothing tells them so
fieldValues.statement: In the essay editor, clicking a paragraph replaces the formatted text with its raw markdown source, and there are no formatting controls: typing markdown is the only way to make a heading, a list, a link or bold text. The help never says this (no help record mentions markdown); the one explanation is a cheat-sheet behind a header action labelled 'Markdown help', which helps only someone who already knows the word. A writer who does not know markdown sees stray symbols in their own text and has no way to format it. This is a different context from the structured editors, where types and fields carry the structure and markdown is only for simple text: the essay offers only paragraph types, and its writer is someone trying to write and own their words, so the plain-text surface stands between them and the writing. Sibling of SP-130 (a first-time writer does not know what to do in the editor): that problem is explaining the editor's concepts, this one is a skill the editor silently requires.
